title: 10 Best No-Code CRM Builders for 2026
summary: Compare 10 no-code CRM builders by data model, workflows, integrations, and security to choose the best fit for your team.
body_markdown:
**Need the short answer?** If I were picking from this list, I’d start with **[Jet Admin](https://www.jetadmin.io/)** for SQL/API-backed internal CRMs, **Softr** for client portals, **Bubble** for deep custom logic, and **Glide** for simple mobile CRM apps.


No-code CRM tools are now a mainstream option. The article points to **[Gartner](https://www.gartner.com/en/about) ’s 70% forecast for new enterprise apps by 2026** and highlights that teams can ship internal apps **up to 5x faster** with about **75% lower cost** than custom builds.


Here’s what I’d look at first:


- **Data model:** Can I handle contacts, accounts, deals, and activities cleanly?
- **Workflows:** Do I need basic triggers or multi-step approvals?
- **Integrations:** Will it connect to SQL, spreadsheets, and[REST APIs](https://www.jetadmin.io/integrations/rest-api) ?
- **Security:** Do I need **RBAC** , **SSO** , audit logs, or private deployment?
- **Deployment:** Cloud-only, self-hosted, on-prem, or air-gapped?


This list covers **10 tools** : **Jet Admin,[Airtable](https://www.airtable.com/) ,[monday CRM](https://monday.com/crm) , Zite,[Knack](https://www.knack.com/) , Softr,[Zoho Creator](https://www.zoho.com/creator/) ,[Caspio](https://www.caspio.com/) , Bubble, and Glide** .

That’s the core of the article in plain English before getting into each tool.


## 1.[Jet Admin](https://www.jetadmin.io/)


**Best for:** Teams building a CRM on an existing database or API.


Jet Admin is a strong fit for teams that want to put a CRM layer on top of data they already have. Instead of starting from scratch, you can build around your current systems and get to a working front end much faster. Jet Admin scores **90/100** for CRM management.


It covers the main parts most teams expect in a CRM, including **contacts, accounts, deals, and activities** . And for teams using internal tool builders like Jet Admin, the payoff can be big: delivery speeds of **up to 5x faster** and cost savings of about **75%** compared with custom development.


### CRM data model


Jet Admin lets you build CRM apps on top of data sources you may already use, such as **Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB, Google Sheets, Airtable,** or a **REST API** .


### Automation & workflows


Jet Admin supports **[workflows and approvals](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/approval-workflow-software-build-secure-automated-approvals-on-your-existing-data/)** , which matters if your CRM needs more than simple record tracking. The free **Internal Tools** plan also includes **unlimited workflows** .


### Integrations & data sources


Jet Admin connects with a broad set of databases and tools, including:


- Postgres
- MySQL
- MongoDB
- [Supabase](https://supabase.com/)
- [Firebase](https://firebase.google.com/)
- Google Sheets
- Airtable
- HubSpot
- [Stripe](https://stripe.com/payments)
- REST APIs


For teams with data locked behind the company firewall, **Jet Bridge** adds access through a secure proxy.


### Security & deployment


On the security side, Jet Admin includes **RBAC** , **SSO via SAML and[Okta](https://www.okta.com/solutions/iam-identity-and-access-management/)** , **audit logs** , and **activity logs** . That makes it a fit for teams that need tighter access control and a clear record of who did what.


Deployment is also flexible. You can run Jet Admin in the cloud, in a self-hosted **VPC** , on-premises, or in **air-gapped environments** .


Pricing depends on the plan. The **Customer Portal Enterprise** plan costs **$649/month** , billed annually, and includes **on-premises setup** , **SAML/Okta SSO** , and a **99.9% SLA** . The **Internal Tools Enterprise** plan uses custom pricing and includes **unlimited apps** plus a **dedicated success manager** .


## 2.[Airtable](https://www.airtable.com/)


**Best for:** Teams that want a flexible, spreadsheet-style CRM built on linked records.


Airtable gives you a spreadsheet-style CRM built around linked tables. That means you can model contacts, companies, deals, and activities in a way that feels familiar at first glance, but has much more structure under the hood.


If your team likes working in spreadsheets but needs more than rows and columns, Airtable sits in that middle ground nicely. You can switch between Kanban, grid, and gallery views based on how your team tracks the pipeline.


### CRM data model


Airtable’s linked-table setup makes it simple to connect contacts, companies, deals, and activities without code. Instead of keeping everything in one messy sheet, you can split data into related tables and tie records together cleanly.


On Enterprise Scale, a base supports up to **500,000 records** . That said, bad data hygiene can slow things down as usage grows. The upside is that this structure also makes CRM updates easier to automate when records change.


### Automation & workflows


Airtable’s native automations can handle pipeline stage changes and follow-up tasks. The limits depend on your plan: the Free plan includes **100 runs per month** , while Business goes up to **100,000** . If you want more advanced logic, you’ll need a paid tier.


Those automations become much more useful once Airtable is tied into the rest of your stack. On its own, it can move records and trigger tasks. Connected to other tools, it can do a lot more.


### Integrations & data sources


Airtable connects with more than **1,500 apps** .


### Security & deployment


Airtable is cloud-only, with no self-hosted or on-premises deployment option. It includes RBAC, while deeper admin controls are limited to higher tiers. SSO is available on the Business plan at **$45/seat/month** , and advanced governance features plus audit logs are usually reserved for enterprise plans.


That pricing ladder matters. Teams with strict governance needs, compliance demands, or a larger user base will likely need those upper-tier controls. For smaller teams, the lower plans may be enough, but the cloud-only setup can be a dealbreaker if on-premises deployment is a hard requirement.


Governance and scale improve as you move up plan tiers.

## 3.[monday CRM](https://monday.com/crm)


**Best for:** Sales teams that want a ready-to-use CRM with minimal setup time.


If your team wants a CRM that feels ready on day one, monday CRM gives you a head start. Instead of starting with a spreadsheet-like setup and building everything from scratch, you get a prebuilt sales setup out of the box. That makes it a good fit for teams that want to move fast and for companies already working inside monday's workspace.


In plain terms: if speed matters more than designing every field and relationship yourself, monday CRM makes that tradeoff pretty easy.


### CRM data model


monday CRM includes a prebuilt sales setup for contacts, deals, and task tracking. So teams can get started fast without mapping out the schema from zero. It also supports automations and dashboards for follow-up tracking,[visual pipeline](https://www.jetadmin.io/templates/sales-pipeline) visibility, and team reporting.


### Integrations & data sources


Teams already using monday can turn it into a structured home base for client data, pipeline tracking, and related workflows.


If your team wants a different mix of structure and flexibility, the next option gives you more room to configure things your way.


## 4. Zite


**Best for:** Teams that want a working CRM app fast from plain-English prompts, without having to[map out the data model](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/how-to-create-a-crm/) first.


Zite turns prompts into a first CRM draft, including leads, accounts, deal stages, contacts, and activities. In plain terms, it helps teams get something usable on the screen fast. That makes it a good fit when speed matters more than getting every detail right on day one. Alternatively, you can start with a[custom CRM template](https://www.jetadmin.io/templates/crms) to get a structured foundation immediately.


### CRM data model


The first draft often needs cleanup before it’s ready for production. Teams usually have to fix field types, tighten relationships, and clean up places where the prompt was read the wrong way.


### Automation & workflows


Workflow depth is not documented here. Before you move ahead, check what Zite supports for triggers, actions, approvals, and follow-up steps.


### Integrations & data sources


Connector details are not documented here. If you plan to use Zite with current data, confirm support for SQL databases, spreadsheets, and REST APIs first.


### Security & deployment


Security and deployment details are not documented here. Confirm RBAC, SSO, audit logs, and whether Zite offers self-hosted or private deployment options directly with Zite.


Zite works best as a fast first draft when your team can review, test, and refine the app afterward. Before rollout, make sure the missing technical and governance details are checked.


## 5.[Knack](https://www.knack.com/)


**Best for:** Teams building structured, database-first CRMs for contact directories and account records.


If your team wants a CRM with a stricter data setup, Knack leans hard into relational data and permission controls. It works well for CRMs built around contacts, accounts, and linked records, where clean database design matters. The upside is simple: field types stay locked down, so stages and statuses don't drift into messy free-text entries.


### Automation & workflows


Knack supports automated triggers and scheduled workflows on paid plans.


### Integrations & data sources


Knack includes a connector library for linking with external data sources and APIs. That said, connector access sits behind paid plans, so it's smart to check the exact APIs and data sources you need before you commit.


### Security & deployment


Knack includes authentication, role permissions, analytics, monitoring, and deployment controls. The free trial is a good way to test the data model and interface first, then switch on paid logic, automation, and integrations once you're sure the setup fits.

## 6. Softr


**Best for:** Teams building[client-facing portals](https://www.jetadmin.io/customer-portal) or light internal CRMs on top of data they already use.


If your team already keeps CRM data in Airtable, Google Sheets, HubSpot, or SQL, Softr helps turn that data into a front end with permissions built in. It’s geared toward[branded client portals](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/client-portal-how-to-design-secure-and-launch-a-portal-your-customers-actually-use/) and light internal CRMs that sit on top of existing systems.


### CRM data model


Softr gives you two paths: use its native relational database or sync with outside data sources in both directions. That means contacts, accounts, and deal stages can stay in Airtable or a SQL database, while Softr displays everything in a clean interface with role-based access.


In plain English: sales reps, managers, and clients can all use the same app, but each person only sees what they’re allowed to see.


### Automation & workflows


Softr comes with built-in workflows for onboarding, request intake, approvals, and notifications. It also supports action buttons, form submissions, and links with[Zapier](https://zapier.com/) and Make when you need more complex logic.


It handles common CRM triggers well. That makes Softr a strong option when the CRM needs a polished interface, not just workflow logic.


### Integrations & data sources


Softr connects with HubSpot, monday.com, ClickUp,[Notion](https://www.notion.com/) , SmartSuite, PostgreSQL, and MySQL, along with Airtable and Google Sheets.


That setup works well if you want to turn data from tools your team already uses into a branded CRM experience.


### Security & deployment


Softr uses server-side auth plus page-, block-, and record-level RBAC, so users only see the data they have permission to access. It also includes SOC 2 and GDPR compliance, while SSO is available on Enterprise plans.


For deployment, Softr supports web apps, PWA use, and custom domains. It stands out most for external-facing CRM setups where tight access control matters.


## 7.[Zoho Creator](https://www.zoho.com/creator/)


**Best for:** Teams building structured, form-based internal CRM apps with strong control over data models and workflow logic.


Zoho Creator is a good fit for teams that want tighter control over records and workflow rules. It’s a low-code platform built for form-based internal apps, including CRM systems.


### CRM data model


You set up the main modules and related modules yourself. That gives you direct control over how contacts, accounts, deals, and activities link together. It also lets you shape record permissions in a more exact way.


The visual builder handles the core setup. And if you want a head start, Zia can generate apps and forms from a prompt.


### Automation & workflows


This is where Zoho Creator can get a bit more hands-on. Complex workflows often depend on Deluge, Zoho’s proprietary scripting language.


So if your CRM needs custom validations, conditional routing, or more advanced record relationships, you’ll probably end up using the scripting layer instead of relying on visual tools alone. That’s not a deal-breaker, but it does mean teams should expect some builder logic to move into code.


### Integrations & data sources


Connection options matter because most CRM setups don’t live on an island. Zoho Creator connects tightly with the Zoho ecosystem, including Zoho CRM and Zoho Books.


It also supports REST API connections and external database integrations. That helps teams pull data from systems outside the Zoho suite when they need to.


### Security & deployment


Zoho Creator includes role-based access control, SSO, and audit logs. Deployment is cloud-based, and enterprise plans add more governance and compliance controls for internal CRM rollouts.


That makes Zoho Creator strongest for teams that care more about structured CRM processes and data control than a polished front end.


## 8.[Caspio](https://www.caspio.com/)


**Best for:** Compliance-sensitive teams that need structured, database-backed CRM apps with granular access controls.


Caspio is built for database-connected apps, so it works well for CRM systems that need contacts, accounts, deals, activities, and support records stored in a relational setup. Its built-in Microsoft SQL Server backend supports unlimited custom fields, along with one-to-many and many-to-many relationships between CRM objects. That makes Caspio a strong option for teams that care about strict governance and clean, structured data.


### CRM data model


Caspio is designed for relational CRM apps. You can use unlimited custom fields and set up one-to-many or many-to-many relationships across contacts, accounts, deals, and support records.


### Automation & workflows


App triggers and scheduled jobs can handle approvals, task updates, and record changes. The low-code app layer gives teams forms, reports, and dashboards, which helps turn database records into day-to-day CRM tools. Caspio's Triggered Actions can also add custom logic for approvals and record updates when a workflow needs more control.


### Integrations & data sources


Caspio keeps CRM data in a live database, so updates happen on an ongoing basis. As contacts, deals, and support cases change over time, records stay current.


### Security & deployment


For compliance-focused teams, Caspio offers granular RBAC at both the page and field levels. It also includes SSO integration and directory-driven provisioning for user lifecycle management. That setup gives admins tight control over who can see or change what.


There is a trade-off, though. Complex workflows and UI changes need to follow Caspio's component-based UI model.


If interface flexibility matters more than strict database control, the next builders lean in that direction.


## 9. Bubble


**Best for:** Teams that need a deeply custom CRM interface and complex business logic.


Bubble is a good fit for teams that want full control over how their CRM looks and works, much like other[production-grade no-code platforms](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/no-code-platform-from-ai-prompt-to-production-grade-business-apps/) . You’re not boxed into preset layouts or fixed templates. Instead, you start with a blank canvas and get pixel-level control over the interface and responsive behavior. That makes Bubble a strong pick when UI flexibility matters more than having a ready-made CRM structure.


### CRM data model


Bubble comes with a built-in relational database, so you can model contacts, accounts, deals, activities, and custom objects right inside the app. You can also define relationships between records, which lets you shape the data model around the way your team actually works.


### Automation & workflows


Bubble’s workflow engine can handle multi-step logic, conditional rules, and automated triggers for things like lead routing, status changes, and reminders. The tradeoff is that setting up and maintaining those workflows often takes developer-level skill.


### Integrations & data sources


Bubble’s API Connector lets you connect to services that offer REST APIs, and its plugin marketplace adds support for payments, analytics, and data syncing. One thing to watch: file storage can get pricey in high-volume apps, so some CRM setups may need external storage integrations.


### Security & deployment


Bubble supports granular role-based access rules and database-level privacy rules, so users only see the records they’re allowed to access. Plan access matters here, especially if you need more control over governance features.

## 10. Glide


**Best for:** Field teams and light internal use cases that need a fast, mobile-friendly CRM built on top of existing spreadsheets.


If your team already keeps CRM data in spreadsheets and just needs a simple app on top of it, Glide is one of the lightest options on this list. It works well for simple, mobile-first CRMs built on Google Sheets, Airtable, or Excel. The main appeal is speed: you can give people access to CRM data fast without setting up a more involved system.


That also means Glide is a better fit when you *don't* need deep workflow logic. Think quick record lookups, basic updates, and a clean mobile front end for data that already exists.


### CRM data model


Glide works as a UI layer on top of **Google Sheets, Airtable, or Excel** , turning rows and columns into a mobile CRM interface. It also comes with **Glide Tables** , a built-in relational database for teams that don't want to manage an external spreadsheet.


If you're starting from scratch, Glide also offers[prebuilt templates for simple CRMs](https://www.jetadmin.io/templates/sales-crm) and directories. That helps you get a basic data model up and running without much setup.


### Automation & workflows


Glide includes action buttons, forms, and basic automations. But it doesn't handle multi-step CRM workflows.


So where does that leave it? Glide makes sense for simple record updates and light pipeline tracking. If your CRM needs approvals, branching logic, or lots of process rules, you'll probably hit its limits pretty fast.


### Integrations & data sources


Glide connects natively with Google Sheets, Airtable, and Microsoft Excel. API access is available on the Business and Enterprise plans.


For desktop use, **Glide Pages** can power dashboards, directories, and portals. That's handy if your team needs both mobile access in the field and a browser-based view back at a desk.


### Security & deployment


Glide supports user authentication and **role-based permissions** . Apps run as **Progressive Web Apps (PWAs)** , which makes Glide a strong match for phone and tablet use.


That's a big part of the pitch here: no heavy app rollout, no clunky mobile experience, just a browser-based app that feels close to native on the devices field teams already carry.

## Pros, Cons, and Final Recommendation


Here’s the short version for the strongest fits in this roundup.


Start with the way you plan to build: a database-backed CRM, a portal, custom app logic, or a mobile tool for field work.

Once you lay out those tradeoffs, the decision usually comes down to three things: **where your data lives** , **how much control you need** , and **how far your workflows need to go** .


If your CRM already runs on existing databases or APIs, **Jet Admin** is the strongest fit for a governed internal app. If your team needs fast mobile updates in the field, **Glide** is the quickest path from rows to a working CRM. If you're building a[client-facing portal](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/client-portal-design-how-to-build-a-secure-intuitive-portal-in-2026/) , **Softr** is the cleanest match. And if you need deep app logic plus tight UI control, **Bubble** gives you the most room to build - but the learning curve is real.


## FAQs


### How do I choose the right no-code CRM builder for my team?


Start with your data architecture. Pick a builder that connects straight to your databases, APIs, or SaaS tools if your customer data lives in more than one place.


Then look at **security** and ease of use. If you work in a regulated industry, check for role-based access control, SSO, SAML, and audit logs. You’ll also want to weigh your team’s technical capacity, how much customization you need, and whether the platform can keep up as the business grows and workflows get more complex.


### Can I build a CRM on top of my existing database or API?


Yes. Jet Admin can build a CRM on top of your current database or API, so you don’t have to move everything into a new system.


It supports API connections, including authentication, rate limits, and pagination. You can use a live connection or scheduled imports, then build CRM screens and workflows around that data. That includes read-only setups, as well as write actions with conflict and error handling.


### Which no-code CRM builders support enterprise security needs?


Several no-code CRM builders can meet enterprise security demands. The focus here is on governance, authentication, and deployment control.


**Jet Admin** includes SAML and Okta SSO, granular **RBAC** down to the row and column level, audit logs, and deployment options for private, local, or fully air-gapped setups.


**[Formaloo](https://www.formaloo.com/)** offers SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and HIPAA compliance.


**Softr** supports SOC 2, GDPR, and server-side authentication.
